subject: double and leading underscores (from Eigen list)

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: double and leading underscores (from Eigen list)
parts:
See the message from Eigen below the sig.

I had no idea about this convention, but it looks like we
should:

* rename all variables that begin with underscores

* rename all variables with double underscores

The first is an internal implementation detail that's pretty
easy to fix.

The second is a big fix requiring messing with the generated
code. It also forces the lp__ fix.

Should we aim for 2.0?

I could turn my attention from the Cholesky factor (which is
independent and can wait to be generalized) to this.

C++ sure is messy (edited for publication from what I
really think).

- Bob


MESSAGE FROM EIGEN:

On Tue, Jul 30, 2013 at 8:10 AM, Hauke Heibel <hauke....@gmail.com> wrote:

> I want to suggest that we refrain from using leading underscores in the
> future because of clause 17.4.3.1.2/1 which states that ...
>
> Certain sets of names and function signatures are always reserved to the
> implementation:
>
> * Each name that contains a double underscore (_ _) or begins with an
> underscore followed by an upper-case letter (2.11) is reserved to the
> implementation for any use.
> * Each name that begins with an underscore is reserved to the implementation
> for use as a name in the global namespace.
>
> In particular the first bullet point can lead to issues and did so on Cygwin
> which did not like the variable name _X. My suggestion to completely stop
> using leading underscores is just a precaution in order to prevent any
> future issues.

I agree, we've been too easy on that. A simple:

grep -e "[ (,_]_[a-zA-Z0-9]" Eigen/* -R

tells me there are numerous such occurences!

gael

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] double and leading underscores (from Eigen list)
parts:
I would file this under the "nice to work towards and cleanup as we can, but not critical" heading and put it off until after 2.0 because:

1) we've not seen any problems due to our use of this,
2) it sounds like Eigen hasn't seen any big problems either, they're just being pedantic and precautionary, and
3) variable names with leading/trailing underscores is a widely used convention so, regardless of what any standard says, it's unlikely that a compiler will all the sudden completely choke on this.

That said, given the version number bump, getting rid of lp__ would be nice to do before 2.0.

Cheers,
Marcus
